subproblem.title: A finite-mass current on ℝ^P is represented by a finite measure concentrated on its support
subproblem.statement: Assume, as hypotheses of the statement, (VO), the frozen type of Submission.dtc_vanish_off_support: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) whose tsupport is disjoint from spt S, S(ω) = 0; and (REP), the frozen type of Submission.cmc_exists_massRepresentation: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with M_W(T) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U (CompactlyContained), there are a measure μ on ℝ^P and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n with μ(ℝ^P \ U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, M_W(T) = μ(W) for every open W, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x and α, T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), and, if moreover boundaryMassOn T W < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U, μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0. Let P, k ∈ ℕ and X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) with M(X) < ∞. Then there are a measure μ on ℝ^P and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_k such that: (1) μ is a finite measure (IsFiniteMeasure); (2) ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable; (3) for μ-a.e. x, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every k-covector α; (4) X(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P); (5) M_W(X) = μ(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P; (6) μ(ℝ^P \ spt X) = 0. Conventions (as in the frozen contract and SimonGMT Chapter06): ℝ^P = Euclid P (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)). For U ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟^k(U) = TestFormOn U k (smooth k-forms on ℝ^P whose compact tsupport lies in U) and 𝒟_k(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U k; X(ω) is the value of X on ω; X − Y is the contract subtraction, (X − Y)(ω) = X(ω) − Y(ω) (definitional); 0 is the zero current; ∂X = X.boundary with ∂X(η) = X(dη) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply); currents with equal values are equal (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). Λ_k = MultiVector P k (continuous linear functionals on k-covectors) and |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α (Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector). M_G(X) = X.massOn G ∈ [0, ∞] is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) over the ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (massAdmissibleOn U k G); M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X); boundaryMassOn X G = M_G(∂X) if k ≥ 1 and 0 if k = 0. spt X = X.support = U \ X.zeroRegion, where X.zeroRegion is the union of the open W with compact closure contained in U on which X vanishes (X(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W). Integrals ∫_E g dμ are Bochner integrals over μ⌞E; {d < t} abbreviates {x : d(x) < t}.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0) → (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → T.massOn W < ∞) → ∃ (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), μ Uᶜ = 0 ∧ (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) ∧ (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = μ W) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ ∧ (∀ (x : Euclid P) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μ) ∧ ((∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → boundaryMassOn T W < ∞) → ∀ E : Set (Euclid P), μHE[n] E = 0 → μ E = 0)) → ∀ (P k : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k), X.mass < ∞ → ∃ (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P k), IsFiniteMeasure μ ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) k, |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k, X ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ) ∧ (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → X.massOn W = μ W) ∧ μ X.supportᶜ = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent-supplied proof of cmcsd_shell_decomposition (the measure (μ_∂, ξ_∂) of ∂T), Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, proof of the deformation theorem 5.1, displays (8)–(10) (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1405–1928). Sibling used: null_off_support (cmcsd_sh_measure_compl_support_eq_zero).
1. For every W ⊆ ℝ^P, M_W(X) ≤ M_{ℝ^P}(X) = M(X) < ∞ (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono, W ⊆ ℝ^P). In particular M_W(X) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ ℝ^P.
2. Apply (REP) with U := ℝ^P (open), n := k and the current X; its hypothesis is step 1. It gives a measure μ and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_k with: M_W(X) = μ(W) for every open W, which is (5); ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, which is (2); |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x and α; and X(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P), which is (4). The other conclusions of (REP) are not needed.
3. ((1).) With W := ℝ^P (open), μ(ℝ^P) = M_{ℝ^P}(X) = M(X) < ∞, so μ is a finite measure (IsFiniteMeasure.mk).
4. ((3).) The bound of step 2 holds for every x, in particular for μ-a.e. x (Filter.Eventually.of_forall).
5. ((6).) By (5), the sibling null_off_support applies to X and μ; with (VO) it gives μ(ℝ^P \ spt X) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: M_W(X) ≤ M(X) < ∞ for every W (massOn_mono), so (REP) applies with U = ℝ^P.
(REP) gives μ, ξ with M_W(X) = μ(W) for open W, a.e. strong measurability, the pointwise bound and X(ω) = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ.
μ(ℝ^P) = M(X) < ∞, so μ is finite; the everywhere bound holds μ-a.e.
null_off_support with (VO) gives μ(ℝ^P \ spt X) = 0.

audit.reason: Global finite mass implies the local hypotheses required by REP. Its open-set equality gives a finite representing measure, its pointwise bound implies the required a.e. bound, and null_off_support supplies concentration. The optional boundary-mass hypothesis of REP is correctly unused.
